accuracy.reason: Eight objectives accurately cover server relational fit, exact constraint/null behavior, scoped ACID, MVCC and conditional stock update, query/index plans, WAL/replicas/partition policy, operational costs and integrated design. PostgreSQL primary passages confirm the critical concurrency and constraint claims.

evidence.quote: Choose the database from access patterns, correctness rules and deployment needs.

mechanisms.reason: Learner can trace the unsafe double-check and safe conditional decrement with affected-row check plus order in the same transaction. Snapshot, commit, index access, replay lag and failover authority each connect state to consequence. Diagram SQL and outcome branches match this boundary.

evidence.quote: Define the rules before relying on the database to preserve them.

coherence.reason: All card prerequisites are ordered: relational model to constraints/ACID, then competing transactions, access paths, replicas and operation/design synthesis. SQL and transaction vocabulary are explicitly prerequisite; new MVCC/WAL/lag terms are introduced.

evidence.quote: The transaction boundary protects its database work; correct rules and concurrency behavior still matter.

decisions.reason: Server versus embedded fit, stronger isolation/retry, index write/storage cost, sync wait versus loss exposure and primary write bottleneck are explicit. Final design elicits unknown load/freshness/loss/recovery targets before claiming sufficiency.

evidence.quote: Use the transaction, update condition, and isolation behavior together to protect the last item.

clarity.reason: Constraint null caveats are precise without drowning the example. Relevant PostgresDiagram and shared renderer/CSS inspected: transaction, stock result, index suitability and stale-copy figures match text. No runtime or database execution claimed.

evidence.quote: Design the query first, then evaluate an index that supports it.

outcomes.reason: Criteria 1-7 satisfied: learner describes SQL client-server relationships/joins/transactions and alternatives; correctly defines primary/unique/not-null/foreign/check including null handling, required reference/quantity choices and limits of enforced rules. Slides 1-2 support all.

Criteria 1-8 satisfied: learner explains ACID database boundary, configured durability/external action exclusion, MVCC snapshots and statement-level Read Committed, check-then-write race and safe conditional decrement/result/order/rollback handling, waits/rechecks and retry limits. Alternative locking syntax is optional.

Criteria 1-9 satisfied: learner proposes account/time access pattern by transfer, EXPLAIN/measurement and scan/index trade-offs, defines WAL/primary/standby and receive/replay lag, contrasts ack waits/loss and explains partition-time authority/promotion/routing rather than universal CP/AP. Transport/config details not required.

Criteria 1-8 satisfied: learner bounds connections, distinguishes replicas/history and restore testing, accounts index/replica/primary costs, proposes required relational constraints and conditional transactional stock/order, validates query/index and elicits freshness/loss/latency/recovery before choosing failover/backups. Slides 2-8 support it.

sourceChecks.claim: Live PostgreSQL Concepts explains relational storage; connection configuration confirms server client connections. Deployment alternatives are scoped workload decisions.

Live Constraints confirms CHECK true-or-null, NOT NULL, default distinct nulls in UNIQUE, primary unique/non-null and foreign-key reference semantics; supports invalid-statement and business-rule boundaries.
Live Transactions tutorial defines all-or-nothing commit/rollback; isolation documentation distinguishes levels. Separate HTTP effects and backup protection are outside this database boundary.

Live Read Committed section confirms per-statement snapshots, updater waiting and WHERE re-evaluation after concurrent commit. Serializable documentation requires aborted-transaction retries; supports the conditional allocation mechanism.
Live Index Introduction confirms access structures and write maintenance; Using EXPLAIN primary followup confirms planner-selected steps and measured plans. No forced-index guarantee is taught.

Previously inspected live warm-standby passages confirm WAL receive/replay, async loss window, configured synchronous stage/count and cost; failover documentation requires exclusive primary authority. CAP followups support scoped partition trade-off.

Live continuous-archiving documents retained historical WAL/PITR and restore process; connection configuration confirms increasing max_connections allocates resources. Warm-standby/index passages support replica/write/maintenance costs.
PostgreSQL Concepts plus verified constraints, isolation, indexes and recovery support this requirements-to-mechanisms synthesis; no unverified benchmark or automatic scale guarantee.
